clue.text: Quiet historian losing footing on edges of ruin

indicators.note: a word's footing is its base, so losing it means dropping the final letter
the edges of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

blocks.note: Tacitus was the Roman historian of the early empire
the first and last letters of ruin

explanation.surface: A historian goes quiet after slipping at the edge of an ancient ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: TACITUS drops its last letter S to give TACITU, then RN completes TACITURN.
explanation.definitionFit: A taciturn person says very little, so the adjective is a synonym for quiet in temperament.

clue.text: Slothful extremes of island life

blocks.note: first and last letters of island
first and last letters of life

explanation.surface: Island living at its laziest, lounging about at the far ends of the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle and slothful both describe someone lazy who avoids work or effort.

clue.text: Maidens periodically need bluesy tunes

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden is an over with no runs scored, recorded as M on the scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: A medley is a musical piece stringing together several songs or tunes in sequence.

clue.text: Scientist loves squeezing large marrow

explanation.walkthrough: Marrow looks like the vegetable but means the central point, as in the marrow of an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: An ologist is an informal word for any specialist in an -ology, a branch of science.

clue.text: Seniors righted a wrong

clue.text: Turns section of poultry farm into co-op?

explanation.definitionFit: A handbell is a small bell rung by hand, struck to sound and so counted among percussion instruments.

clue.text: Ecstasy and anger in Ireland

ire, wrath

clue.text: Eccentric horologer with a wind problem

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Logorrhoea is excessive talkativeness, and wind is idle verbose chatter, so the condition is a problem of too much talk.

clue.text: After change of leader, several become exhausted

blocks.note: sundry means various or several

clue.text: Roman emperor, regularly ignoring advisor, called time on Scotsman

explanation.walkthrough: Called looks like the start of called time, but its letters join advisor in the alternating run.
explanation.definitionFit: Diocletian ruled Rome from 284 to 305 and divided the empire into a tetrarchy.

clue.text: Old ducks spell trouble for gastropod

explanation.definitionFit: A sea snail is a marine mollusc with a coiled shell, one of the many kinds of gastropod.

clue.text: Our sort of environmentalists retired, overwhelmed by burden

blocks.note: FoE is Friends of the Earth, the environmental campaign group
onus, a duty or burden

clue.text: Mum dined merrily, as luminous as ever

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Something undimmed has lost none of its brightness, so it shines as luminously as it always did.

clue.text: Cover skin of backside with trousers, back to front

clue.text: All children tire, lying about

taken as written

clue.text: Married prince leaving old Spanish capital for plateau
